So the job is still dead and its work is still undone: the fence stops a later bulk replay from re-running a poisoned payload, and it fixes nothing about why the payload failed. The bad data, the producer bug or the schema behind it is untouched and a human still has to act. Unlike a pause the fence does not expire, so nothing is on a clock — but 'permanent' describes the fence, not the incident. The underlying fault on 3971a293-3f5b-55eb-b835-649d685801a7 is unchanged and still needs a human decision on the real fix. Treat the stabilization as a clock, not an outcome.
